# Resource: stripe_billing_credit_grant

Billing credits given to a customer. Only `expires_at` and `metadata` can change after creation.

~> Stripe cannot delete a credit grant; set `expires_at` to end one. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the billing credit grant, fail at plan time. To stop managing a billing credit grant, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

resource "stripe_billing_credit_grant" "welcome" {
  name     = "Welcome credit"
  customer = stripe_customer.acme.id
  category = "promotional"

  amount = {
    type = "monetary"
    monetary = {
      currency = "usd"
      value    = 2500
    }
  }

  applicability_config = {
    scope = {
      price_type = "metered"
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount of this credit grant. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`amount`](#amount) below.
* `applicability_config` - (Required) Configuration specifying what this credit grant applies to. We currently only support `metered` prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`applicability_config`](#applicability_config) below.

The following arguments are optional:

* `category` - (Optional) The category of this credit grant. It defaults to `paid` if not specified. Possible values: `paid`, `promotional`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `customer` - (Optional) ID of the customer receiving the billing credits. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `customer_account` - (Optional) ID of the account representing the customer receiving the billing credits. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `effective_at` - (Optional) The time when the billing credits become effective-when they're eligible for use. It defaults to the current timestamp if not specified. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `expires_at` - (Optional) The time when the billing credits expire. If not specified, the billing credits don't expire.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. You can use this to store additional information about the object (for example, cost basis) in a structured format.
* `name` - (Optional) A descriptive name shown in the Dashboard. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `priority` - (Optional) The desired priority for applying this credit grant. If not specified, it will be set to the default value of 50. The highest priority is 0 and the lowest is 100. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

<a id="amount"></a>
### `amount`

The `amount` attribute supports:

* `monetary` - (Optional) The monetary amount. See [`amount.monetary`](#amount.monetary) below.
* `type` - (Required) The type of this amount. We currently only support `monetary` billing credits. Possible values: `monetary`.

<a id="amount.monetary"></a>
### `amount.monetary`

The `amount.monetary` attribute supports:

* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `value` - (Required) A positive integer representing the amount.

<a id="applicability_config"></a>
### `applicability_config`

The `applicability_config` attribute supports:

* `scope` - (Required) See [`applicability_config.scope`](#applicability_config.scope) below.

<a id="applicability_config.scope"></a>
### `applicability_config.scope`

The `applicability_config.scope` attribute supports:

* `price_type` - (Optional) The price type that credit grants can apply to. We currently only support the `metered` price type. This refers to prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Cannot be used in combination with `prices`. Possible values: `metered`.
* `prices` - (Optional) The prices that credit grants can apply to. We currently only support `metered` prices. This refers to prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Cannot be used in combination with `price_type`. See [`applicability_config.scope.prices`](#applicability_config.scope.prices) below.

<a id="applicability_config.scope.prices"></a>
### `applicability_config.scope.prices`

The `applicability_config.scope.prices` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `id` - (Required) Unique identifier for the object.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `test_clock` - ID of the test clock this credit grant belongs to.
* `updated` - Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `voided_at` - The time when this credit grant was voided. If not present, the credit grant hasn't been voided.

## Removing from State

To stop managing a billing credit grant whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome
```

The billing credit grant stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a billing credit grant using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome
  id = "credgr_test_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome
  identity = {
    id = "credgr_test_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the billing credit grant.

Using `terraform import`, import a billing credit grant using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome credgr_test_123
```
